---
title: "Claude setup"
description: "Keyless Claude API access for the roxygen and test suggestions and the analysis scripts."
---

The [roxygen](roxygen-suggest.qmd) and [test](test-suggest.qmd)
suggestion workflows and the [analysis scripts](datashield-analysis-suggest.qmd)
call the Claude API **without a stored API key**. They
use [Workload Identity Federation](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation):
the job proves its identity with GitHub's OIDC token and gets a
short-lived Anthropic token in exchange. Nothing secret is stored — the
three IDs below only say *which* rule to use.

The workflows don't come with Claude access: you connect your repositories
to an Anthropic organization of your own, which is billed for their usage.
One organization can serve any number of repositories — the layout below
shows usage per repository.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Want to try it first?
If you'd like to see the suggestions on one of your packages before
setting up an Anthropic organization, send me an e-mail. A trial can run
on an existing organization, with your repository's usage tracked
separately.
:::

## Recommended layout

| In the Claude Console | One per | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Workspace | workflow type — e.g. `suggest-docs`, `suggest-tests`, `suggest-analysis` | Separate usage and spend limits per workflow type |
| Service account | repository | The *Cost* page can group by service account, i.e. by repository |
| Federation rule | repository × workflow | Each rule only admits one workflow file of one repository |

## Setting up a repository

In the Claude Console under **Settings → Workload identity**:

1. **Workspaces** — create a workspace once for each workflow type you
   use: the two package workflows, and the analysis scripts if you use
   them.
2. **Service account** — create one for the repository and add it to each
   workspace it uses.
3. **Federation rules** — create one per workflow, with GitHub Actions as
   the provider and, under *Match configuration*, a **CEL expression**:

   ```
   claims.repository_owner_id == "<owner id>" && claims.repository_id == "<repository id>" && claims.job_workflow_ref.startsWith("nfdi4health/datashield-workflows/.github/workflows/roxygen-suggest.yml@")
   ```

   (or `test-suggest.yml` for the test rule,
   `datashield-analysis-suggest.yml` for the analysis rule).
   - *Target*: the repository's service account, in the matching workspace.
   - The two IDs are numbers: `owner.id` and `id` in
     `https://api.github.com/repos/<owner>/<repo>`. They keep the rule to
     your one repository — a fork has another ID, and a rename doesn't
     change it.
   - `startsWith(…@")` admits that workflow at any version: `@main`,
     `@v1`, or a branch you test with — no rule change when you switch.
   - No subject is checked, so the rule works for both of GitHub's
     subject formats (repositories created after mid-2026 get one with
     IDs).
4. **Secrets** — store in the repository:

   | Secret | Value |
   |---|---|
   | `ANTHROPIC_ORG_ID` | Your organization ID — can be one organization-level secret |
   | `ANTHROPIC_SVAC_ID` | The service account's `svac_...` ID |
   | `ANTHROPIC_FDRL_ROXYGEN` | The roxygen rule's `fdrl_...` ID |
   | `ANTHROPIC_FDRL_TESTS` | The test rule's `fdrl_...` ID |
   | `ANTHROPIC_FDRL_ANALYSIS` | The analysis rule's `fdrl_...` ID (analysis projects) |

::: {.callout-warning}
## Don't mix up the rule IDs
Each rule only accepts its own workflow file. Passing the roxygen rule's ID
to the test workflow (or the other way round) fails at the token exchange.
This is also why the callers map secrets explicitly instead of using
`secrets: inherit`.
:::

The caller job needs `id-token: write` to request the OIDC token; the
example callers already include it.

::: {.callout-note}
## Rules from before the move
Rules created with a subject prefix and an exact `job_workflow_ref` claim
(`…@refs/heads/main`) only admit `@main` of the old path
`FlorianSchw/package-workflows`. Change them to the expression above:
rules can be edited, and their `fdrl_…` IDs stay the same, so your
secrets don't change.
:::
